results.content:
# How Much Does Big E Parking Cost?  
Published on [Alec Pow](https://www.thepricer.org/alec-pow/)
This article was researched using 5 sources. See our [methodology](https://www.thepricer.org/methodology/) and [corrections policy](https://www.thepricer.org/corrections/).  
The Big E, officially the Eastern States Exposition, is one of the largest fairs in the United States and a major draw for New England residents each fall. Held in West Springfield, Massachusetts, the event attracts over a million visitors across its two-week run. With such huge crowds, one of the most pressing questions for attendees is how much parking will cost and what options are available. Parking costs can shape a family’s budget, influence arrival time, and even determine whether visitors drive or take a shuttle.  
For many attendees, the parking fee is the first price they encounter before even stepping through the gates. Understanding the full range of fees helps avoid surprises at the lot and allows better planning for multi-day trips or larger vehicles. Below, we look at the different categories of parking at The Big E, real-world examples of costs, and the hidden fees that may impact the total.
## **How Much Does Big E Parking Cost?**  
Parking at The Big E is straightforward, but it comes with variations depending on the type of vehicle. As of 2024–2025, the official **Big E parking costs are** **$10 (about 20 minutes at $30 per hour) for cars and trucks**, **$5 for motorcycles**, and **$20 for campers or oversized vehicles**. The most common payment method remains cash at the gate, especially at the main entrance, Gate 9, though some off-site lots accept cards. These prices have held steady for several seasons, though increased traffic and demand during peak days can make availability more valuable than the face price.  
The Big E does not charge extra for admission parking privileges, but the traffic leading into the fairgrounds means the time cost can be significant. Visitors arriving late in the morning often face heavy congestion on Memorial Avenue, which is the main route into the lots. According to the Massachusetts Department of Transportation (MassDOT, 2023), traffic volumes around the fairgrounds peak between 9 a.m. and noon, leading to added delays and higher stress levels.
## **Cost Breakdown**  
The pricing tiers at The Big E are relatively simple compared with other large state fairs. Here is a clear view of the rates:  
| **Vehicle Type** | **Daily Parking Cost** | **Notes** |
|---|---|---|
| Cars/Trucks | **$10** | Main lots, typically paid at Gate 9 |
| Motorcycles | **$5** | Designated motorcycle zones, closer to entrances |
| Campers/Oversized | **$20** | May incur an extra **$10** if space is exceeded |
| Bicycles | Free | Limited racks available near entrances |  
Vehicle Type Daily Parking Cost Notes Cars/Trucks $10 Main lots, typically paid at Gate 9 Motorcycles $5 Designated motorcycle zones, closer to entrances  
This table reflects official 2024–2025 rates as published by The Eastern States Exposition office (Big E, 2024). Off-site private lots can range between **$5 and $15** depending on distance and whether shuttle service is included.

results.name: A Guide to the Big E: New England's Best Fair (Updated 2026)
results.content:
Don’t you just love attending fairs – especially in the Fall?  
There’s one fair I love in particular that I’ve been attending since I was a little girl: The Big E, a multi-state event representing the 6 New England states, Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Rhode Island, and Vermont.  
This massive fair takes place at the Eastern States Exposition grounds every Fall in West Springfield, Massachusetts.  
If there was ever a time to visit my favorite region of the US, Fall is it!  
The weather is mild, the foliage is painting landscapes with red, orange, and yellow, and there are fairs popping up nearly every weekend in adorable small towns.  
The Big E is like one last outdoors hurrah before the doom and gloom of Winter take over for a few months. It makes for an excellent [day trip from Boston](https://www.frostandsun.com/day-trips-from-boston/) or pit stop on a New England road trip.  
In this guide to the Big E fair in New England, I’ll share the best hotels, parking tips, events to partake in, concerts to scope out, and food to try.  
**Table of contents**  
[hide](#)
## How much does The Big E cost?  
Admission is $20 for adults and $12 for children age 6-12. Children age 5 and under are free.  
A number of discounts are available as follows:  
1. **Adult 2023 season pass**: $70 for unlimited admission in 2023
2. **Child 2023 season pass**: $35 for unlimited admission in 2023
3. **Opening day admission**: $12 (for all ages over 5)
4. **Military Appreciation Day admission**: Free on September 15 (opening day)  
In addition to discount admission, you can save on tickets for rides at the Midway with the Midway Magic Pass.  
The Midway Magic Pass is $35 for unlimited rides Monday through Friday or worth 26 tickets on Saturday and Sunday.
## Do you have any tips for Big E Parking?  
Parking at the Big E can be a bit of a hassle. It fills up super quick and traffic getting out at the end of the night is difficult.  
Official parking is $10 for automobiles in Lot 9. Motorcycles can park in Lot 7 for $5. Bicycles can park in Lot 7 for free.  
Local businesses leading up to the entrance gates often offer parking at an upcharge. Sometimes they allow local organizations or school groups to use their property to fundraise via the parking fee, as well.  
You might be tempted to park and walk to avoid the traffic leading in and out. That’s usually what my family and I end up doing! While it is more expensive than official parking, we don’t mind paying more if it’s going to a local organization or school.

results.name: A Guide To The Big E and RV Rentals | RVshare
results.content:
### HOW TO GET THERE  
The Big E offers free or low-cost weekend shuttles from West Springfield to the fair only. You can use Springfield Union Station’s shuttle service on the weekend. It will arrive at Gate 24 at Springfield Union Station. You can also use the Pioneer Valley Transit Authority buses to get to and from the fair. ● From Connecticut: Take I-91 North from Rte. 2, I-84, I-95, or the Merritt Parkway. Follow I-91 N to MA Exit 3. Take Rte. 5 North to Rte. 147 W, Memorial Ave., about 3/4 mi. to ESE’s Gate 9 parking lot. ● From Boston: Take the Massachusetts Turnpike I-90 W to Exit 45, then take Rte. 5 S to Rte. 147 W. Continue about 3/4 mi. to ESE’s Gate 9 parking lot. ● From Berkshires: Take the Massachusetts Turnpike E to Exit 45, then take Rte. 5 S to Rte. 147 W. Continue about 3/4 mi. to ESE’s Gate 9 parking lot. ● From Vermont: Take I-91 South to Mass. Exit 10B, then take Rte. 5 S to Rte. 147 W. Continue about 3/4 mi. to ESE’s Gate 9 public parking lot.
### PARKING  
Parking is available on the grounds at Gate 9, with a cash-only charge. Please note that there are no ATMs near the gate, so be sure to bring cash. Parking fees vary depending on the type of vehicle: cars are $10 per vehicle, motorcycles are $5, and campers are $20 per space per day, with an additional $10 fee for extended awnings or cars occupying adjacent spaces. In addition to the on-site parking, private parking lots are available in the neighborhoods along Memorial Avenue. These lots are not affiliated with The Big E, and the fees are set by the property owners, so prices may vary.
### TICKETS & PRICING  
You can purchase [tickets](https://www.thebige.com/p/buy-tickets) for The Big E online or at the box office. Discounted tickets are available through September 10, 2026, at 11:59 PM. The Advance Discount for Adult 1-Day tickets is $16 (regularly $20 at the gate) for ages 13 and older. The Advance Discount for Child 1-Day tickets is $10 (regularly $12 at the gate) for ages 6 to 12, while children ages 5 and under are free.
